grounding.claim: Role 'Map owner' may do everything 'Map reader' may do
grounding.note: I read the whole request handler (do_GET at 633, do_POST at 654) and grepped the tools tree for authoriz/authenticat/login/rbac/current_user/Authorization: zero hits, so the product has no identity check at all. Every visitor of the loopback server gets the same capabilities, and R2's use cases UC5/UC6 are pure viewer navigation, so the owner can do all of them; the inclusion is true because nothing separates the two people, not because any line grants it - which is why the map anchors it nowhere.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A served map is reachable only from the machine that runs the server.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:885 — Opens the listening address on this machine alone, so a connection from another machine never arrives.
grounding.note: Read line 885: ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), Handler). The bind address is the literal loopback, and it is the only ThreadingHTTPServer construction in the file, so the socket never accepts a connection from another machine.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A served map is reachable only from the machine that runs the server.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:634 — Refuses a page request whose address names any host other than this machine.
grounding.note: Read 633-635 and _loopback_host at 583-594, then ran it: 'evil.com' -> False and '127.0.0.1.evil.com' -> False, while '127.0.0.1:8765', 'localhost' and '[::1]:8765' -> True; a named non-loopback Host gets 403. An ABSENT Host is deliberately allowed (line 588-589), which the claim does not cover but does not contradict.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A served map is reachable only from the machine that runs the server.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:655 — Refuses the same way for a request that changes the remembered project list.
grounding.note: Read 654-667: do_POST's first statement is the same _loopback_host check returning 403, and the only POST routes below it (line 661) are api/open, api/forget and api/reorder - exactly the requests that change the remembered project list.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A project folder is served only when it was deliberately added, never because the server found it.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:883 — Builds the served set from the remembered folder list alone, with no search of the disk.
grounding.note: Read 883 and build_projects at 269-283: it iterates only the folders handed to it and calls load_project on each; there is no glob, walk or scan. I also checked every other assignment to Handler.projects (676, 701, 709, 718) - all of them pass store.list() too.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A project folder is served only when it was deliberately added, never because the server found it.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:697 — Refuses to add a folder that holds no coyodex data folder inside it.
grounding.note: Read _open at 691-702: line 697 calls _has_coyodex(p) and returns 400 'that folder has no .coyodex/ folder' when it is false, before store.add at 700. _has_coyodex (104-111) tests folder/.coyodex is a directory; I ran it on /tmp and got False.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A project folder is served only when it was deliberately added, never because the server found it.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:878 — Applies the same check to a folder named when the server is started.
grounding.note: Read serve() at 869-883: the loop over add_folders (the folders named on the command line) calls store.add only inside 'if _has_coyodex(folder)', and otherwise prints 'skipping <folder> - no .coyodex/ folder' to stderr. Same helper as the _open path.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A project folder is served only when it was deliberately added, never because the server found it.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:658 — Refuses a change to the remembered list unless the request came from this server's own start page.
grounding.note: Read 654-667: every POST is refused with 403 unless the request carries X-Coyodex: serve, and I found the sender - the server's own landing-page script at serve.py:1041 sets that header on its fetches. Precision note: it is a CSRF header, so a local command-line tool can set it too; what it actually refuses is a cross-origin browser page, which combined with the loopback check at 655 is the intent.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A request for a file can only ever reach inside the mapped project's own folder.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:778 — Rejects a file request whose path is absolute or climbs above the project folder.
grounding.note: Read 776-779: the src route takes path from the query string and returns 400 'bad path' when _safe_rel fails. I ran _safe_rel (defined 338-343): '/etc/passwd' -> False, '../../etc/passwd' -> False, 'a/b.py' -> True.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A request for a file can only ever reach inside the mapped project's own folder.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:380 — Rejects a working copy read that escapes the project or names the version history folder.
grounding.note: Read worktree_read at 375-399: line 380 returns None when _safe_rel fails or the first path segment is '.git'. I ran worktree_read against this repo: '../../etc/passwd' -> None, '.git/config' -> None, 'method.md' -> 267483 bytes served.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A request for a file can only ever reach inside the mapped project's own folder.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:387 — Refuses a file whose real location, after following a shortcut, sits outside the project folder.
grounding.note: Read 382-388: the path is resolved with Path.resolve(strict=True), which follows symlinks, and line 387 returns None unless the REAL path is relative to the resolved repo root (and re-checks for a '.git' part). So a tracked symlink pointing outside the project is refused after resolution, not before.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A request for a file can only ever reach inside the mapped project's own folder.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:849 — Hands back a shared page asset only when the requested name is one of the two allowed names.
grounding.note: Read _static at 846-851: the name is looked up in the _STATIC_FILES dict and anything missing gets 404 before _send_file is reached. I printed the dict's keys: exactly ['viewer.css', 'viewer.js'] - two names, so no traversal is possible.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A file that version history deliberately ignores is never handed back to the browser.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:391 — Allows a working copy read when version history already tracks the file.
grounding.note: Read 391-395: 'git ls-files --error-unmatch -- <path>' returning 0 means the file is tracked, and the code then skips the untracked branch entirely and falls through to real.read_bytes(). I ran worktree_read on the tracked '.coyodex/preindex.json' and got 1813114 bytes back.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A file that version history deliberately ignores is never handed back to the browser.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:393 — Allows an untracked file only when no ignore rule covers it.
grounding.note: Read 392-395: for an untracked file the code runs 'git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- <path>' (--exclude-standard applies the ignore rules) and returns None unless the path appears in that output. I ran worktree_read on two gitignored files in this repo, '.claude/settings.local.json' and '.DS_Store', and both came back None.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A version name arriving in a web address is refused unless it reads as an ordinary commit name.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:790 — Refuses a requested version that is not a plain commit identifier.
grounding.note: Read 776-799: 'at' is read straight from the query string at 782, and line 790 returns 400 'bad at= commit' unless _valid_commit passes. I ran _valid_commit: 'HEAD' -> False, '-upload-pack=x' -> False, 'deadbeef' -> True, so only a bare hex SHA reaches git's argv.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A version name arriving in a web address is refused unless it reads as an ordinary commit name.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:366 — Refuses a branch or tag name that opens with a dash or carries unusual characters.
grounding.note: The check itself is real - _safe_ref at 353-357 refused '--upload-pack=x' and 'a b' and accepted 'main' when I ran it. But I opened every call site of this resolve_ref: the ONLY production caller is impact_commits at serve.py:405, which passes proj.commit, a value read from the map file and already forced to a bare SHA by load_project at serve.py:127. No version name arriving in a web address ever reaches line 366. The refs that DO arrive in a web address (base/target at serve.py:819-820) go to a different function, impact_git.resolve_ref, guarded at tools/coyodex/impact_git.py:60, and the src route's at= is guarded at serve.py:790. The rule is enforced, but not here.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A version name arriving in a web address is refused unless it reads as an ordinary commit name.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:368 — Marks where the options end, so the name after it can never be read as one.
grounding.note: Line 368 does pass --end-of-options to git rev-parse, so a ref could not become a flag. Same caller finding as line 366 though: the only production call site of this resolve_ref is impact_commits at serve.py:405, feeding it proj.commit, which load_project already validated as a bare SHA at serve.py:127. The web-address refs go through impact_git.resolve_ref (tools/coyodex/impact_git.py:62, which carries its own --end-of-options), so no name from a web address is protected by line 368.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A version name arriving in a web address is refused unless it reads as an ordinary commit name.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/serve.py:301 — Skips the history read entirely when the map's own recorded commit is not plain.
grounding.note: Read git_ls_files at 299-306: line 301 returns [] before any subprocess call when _valid_commit fails, so no git command runs. I opened the caller, project_tree at serve.py:491, which passes proj.commit - the map's own recorded commit - exactly as the claim says.

grounding.claim: Rule 'Code fetched from the public internet runs in the viewer only when its fingerprint matches the expected one.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/viewer.html:17 — Pins the expected fingerprint of the picture panning library.
grounding.note: Read 13-18: line 16 loads https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom@3.6.1/dist/svg-pan-zoom.min.js and line 17 is its integrity="sha384-yc/c2Lk1s2V2ir1rxvjo8YyVD9PlOlYTqpNr3Wm1WIuAA30GlDYNx6U5104OiavY", with crossorigin="anonymous" on 18 so the browser can check it. svg-pan-zoom is the pan/zoom library for the diagrams.

grounding.claim: Rule 'Code fetched from the public internet runs in the viewer only when its fingerprint matches the expected one.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/viewer.html:20 — Pins the expected fingerprint of the diagram drawing library.
grounding.note: Read 19-21: line 19 loads https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.15.0/dist/mermaid.min.js and line 20 is its integrity="sha384-yQ4mmBBT+vhTAwjFH0toJXNYJ6O4usWnt6EPIdWwrRvx2V/n5lXuDZQwQFeSFydF", crossorigin anonymous on 21. Mermaid is the library that draws the diagrams.

grounding.claim: Rule 'Code fetched from the public internet runs in the viewer only when its fingerprint matches the expected one.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/viewer.js:14094 — Pins the expected fingerprint of the styling that colours source code.
grounding.note: Read ensureHljs at 14090-14103: line 14094 sets css.href = HLJS_CSS and css.integrity = HLJS_CSS_SRI before appending the <link>. HLJS_CSS (14085) is highlight.js 11.9.0's styles/github.min.css from cdnjs - the stylesheet that colours source code - and HLJS_CSS_SRI (14086) is its sha384.

grounding.claim: Rule 'Code fetched from the public internet runs in the viewer only when its fingerprint matches the expected one.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/viewer.js:14097 — Pins the expected fingerprint of the code colouring library itself.
grounding.note: Read 14096-14100: line 14097 sets s.src = HLJS_JS and s.integrity = HLJS_JS_SRI before the script is appended. HLJS_JS (14083) is highlight.js 11.9.0's highlight.min.js from cdnjs and HLJS_JS_SRI (14084) is its sha384; onerror at 14099 just falls back to plain text.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A source link may open only through an address belonging to a known code editor.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/viewer.js:14880 — Offers no link when the built address is not one a known editor answers.
grounding.note: Read editorUri at 14868-14881: line 14880 returns the built URI only when ALLOWED_OPEN_SCHEMES has its scheme, else null. That set (14811-14815) is 23 editor schemes - vscode, cursor, zed, idea, subl, emacs and so on - and the comment says it blocks javascript:/data:/file:/http(s):. I opened the only caller, doOpenSource at 14921-14926: it fires the URI only when non-null and otherwise falls back to the GitHub URL.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A source link may open only through an address belonging to a known code editor.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/viewer/viewer.js:15011 — Refuses to save a hand-typed link pattern whose address is not a known editor one.
grounding.note: Read saveSettings at 15005-15021: when the chosen target is 'custom', line 15011 tests the typed template's scheme against ALLOWED_OPEN_SCHEMES and returns with the message 'Scheme not allowed' BEFORE any lsSet, so an unknown scheme is never stored.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A run refuses to read or overwrite coyodex's own map unless the operator declares coyodex is the project being mapped.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/model.py:1443 — Refuses to read a map stored inside coyodex's own copy unless the run declared that coyodex is the project.
grounding.note: Read resolve_map_path at 1414-1450: unless COYODEX_SELF_MAP is 1/true/yes, a path under COYODEX_HOME/.coyodex raises WrongMapError at 1443. I confirmed it at runtime: 'coyodex dump --map /Users/nitsanseniak/Projects/coyodex/.coyodex/project-map.json --id R1' with the variable unset printed 'ERROR: refusing to read ... that is the COYODEX CLONE'S OWN map'; with COYODEX_SELF_MAP=1 the same command succeeded.

grounding.claim: Rule 'A run refuses to read or overwrite coyodex's own map unless the operator declares coyodex is the project being mapped.' is enforced at tools/coyodex/model.py:1408 — Refuses the same target for a write, so a stray build cannot overwrite the accepted map of coyodex.
grounding.note: Read guard_wrong_map at 1395-1411: it raises WrongMapError at 1408 for the same COYODEX_HOME/.coyodex target, with the same COYODEX_SELF_MAP escape at 1402. I opened its only call site, assemble.py:976 - it runs BEFORE the write at assemble.py:978 and passes no override, and assemble is the only verb that writes a map (grep for guard_wrong_map across tools/ returns just that one caller).

grounding.claim: Rule 'A run refuses to read or overwrite coyodex's own map unless the operator declares coyodex is the project being mapped.' is enforced at method.md:1369 — Tells the build the refusal exists, and warns that a hand written script is not covered by the refusal.
grounding.note: Read method.md 1358-1371. Line 1369 states that coyodex refuses to read the clone's own .coyodex/ unless COYODEX_SELF_MAP=1 is set, 'which catches the verbs', and 1370-1371 warn that a bare python3 heredoc is not a coyodex verb so the rule must still be obeyed rather than relied on - both halves of the claim, word for word.
